title: Rees Modules Artin Rees and Hilbert Samuel Theory

items.title: Nonnegatively graded rings and modules, homogeneous elements, and twists
The Hilbert function and formal Hilbert series of a graded module with finite-length pieces
A finite graded module over a standard graded algebra has rational Hilbert series and eventual polynomial growth
items.strategy: Filter by a degree-one generator, compare successive quotients by multiplication, and induct on the number of degree-one generators to force a rational denominator and eventual polynomial behaviour.

items.title: The associated graded ring and associated graded module of an ideal-adic filtration
The Rees algebra of an ideal and the Rees module of a filtered module
Over a Noetherian ring, an ideal filtration is stable exactly when its Rees module is finite, and the Rees algebra is Noetherian
items.strategy: Translate stability into finite generation in degrees bounded above, then reverse the argument by reading a finite homogeneous generating set back into the filtration.

items.title: Artin-Rees controls intersections of submodules with high ideal powers
items.strategy: Embed the Rees module of the induced filtration on the submodule into the finite Rees module of the ambient module and convert finite homogeneous generation back into the displayed equality.

items.title: The filtration induced on a submodule is equivalent to its intrinsic ideal-adic filtration
items.strategy: Apply Artin-Rees to the ambient ideal-adic filtration and compare the resulting eventual inclusions in both directions.

items.title: The Krull intersection is the $(1-a)$-torsion submodule, and it vanishes in the Jacobson-radical case
items.strategy: Apply Artin-Rees to the submodule given by the intersection of all powers, then use the determinant-trick form of Nakayama on the stable equality and the Jacobson-radical unit criterion for the vanishing clause.

items.title: The Hilbert-Samuel function and eventual Hilbert-Samuel polynomial of a finite local module
The Hilbert-Samuel function agrees eventually with a rational polynomial in binomial form
items.strategy: Apply Hilbert-Serre to the associated graded module over the associated graded ring and recover the cumulative quotient-length function by summing the graded pieces.

items.title: Hilbert-Samuel multiplicity as the factorial-scaled leading coefficient
The degree of the Hilbert-Samuel polynomial equals the dimension of the support
items.strategy: Use Artin-Rees to compare submodules of finite colength, reduce to cyclic quotients, and identify the degree of the Hilbert-Samuel polynomial with the support dimension by induction on dimension.

items.title: For a finite module, the dimension is the least size of an ideal of definition, and such tuples are systems of parameters
items.strategy: Read the dimension theorem on the support of the module against ideals of finite-length quotient and isolate the minimal number of generators needed for an ideal of definition.

items.title: Hilbert-Samuel multiplicity is additive on short exact sequences at the top dimension
items.strategy: Compare the Hilbert-Samuel functions in a short exact sequence, use Artin-Rees to control the induced filtration, and read the top-degree term of the resulting polynomial identity.

items.title: Modulo a parameter preserves the top Hilbert-Samuel multiplicity up to the finite-annihilator correction
items.strategy: Take Euler characteristic of the parameter Koszul complex first in the two-term x direction, producing the quotient contribution in degree zero and the annihilator correction in degree one.

items.title: For a nonzero finite module and an ideal of definition, Hilbert-Samuel multiplicity is a positive integer
items.strategy: Apply the dimension theorem and descend by parameters until the finite-length case, where multiplicity is the positive length of a nonzero Artinian quotient.

title: Rees Modules Artin Rees and Hilbert Samuel Theory — Examples

items.title: The polynomial ring and a homogeneous quotient have the expected Hilbert series and Hilbert polynomial
The associated graded ring of a regular local ring and of a cusp local ring can be computed explicitly
An explicit Artin-Rees number can be computed for a submodule inside a finite module
In a Noetherian local domain, the intersection of the powers of the maximal ideal is zero
A DVR has Hilbert-Samuel polynomial $n+1$ and multiplicity one
The Hilbert-Samuel multiplicity of a plane-curve singularity is read from its associated graded ring
In dimension zero the Hilbert-Samuel polynomial is constant and equals the module length
Direct sums and direct summands of flat modules are flat
items.strategy: Use that tensor products commute with direct sums for the coproduct statement and that a direct summand inherits injectivity preservation from the split inclusion and projection.

items.title: Every localization is flat, and localizing a flat module preserves flatness
items.strategy: Identify localization with tensoring by the localized ring and use the ideal criterion after passing to the exact localized tensor description.

items.title: A module is flat if and only if all prime localizations are flat, equivalently all maximal localizations are flat
items.strategy: Localize the ideal criterion to prove one direction and then detect global injectivity by checking the localized kernels at all maximal ideals.

items.title: The equational criterion characterizes flat modules by lifting finite relations on generators
items.strategy: Translate a relation in the tensor presentation into a kernel element of a map from a finite free module and factor that map through another finite free module that kills the relation.

items.title: If $R/I$ is flat then $I = I^2$, and for finitely generated $I$ this is equivalent to generation by an idempotent
items.strategy: Apply the ideal criterion and the quotient-tensor isomorphism to get I = I^2, then use the determinant trick on the finite ideal to construct its idempotent generator.

items.title: For a flat module, faithful flatness is equivalent to detecting nonzero modules and residue fields
items.strategy: Show that exactness reflection is equivalent to killing no nonzero module, then pass between arbitrary nonzero modules and residue-field fibres by taking annihilator quotients and maximal ideals.

items.title: A flat ring map is faithfully flat exactly when it detects proper ideals and is surjective on spectra
items.strategy: Apply the module characterization of faithful flatness to residue fields and quotient modules, then translate the nonvanishing condition into the existence of primes over every prime and maximal ideal.

items.title: Every faithfully flat ring map is injective
items.strategy: Apply the proper-ideal detection criterion to the zero ideal.

items.title: Flatness descends along faithfully flat base change
items.strategy: Ascend flatness by the published extension-of-scalars theorem, and descend it by testing injectivity after tensoring with a faithfully flat algebra and using the published transitivity statement.

items.title: Finite generation descends along faithfully flat ring maps
items.strategy: Choose generators after base change, descend them modulo maximal ideals in the source, and apply Nakayama to conclude global finite generation.

items.title: For an $R$-finite module over a local map, flatness modulo $I$ and injectivity of $I \\otimes M \\to M$ imply flatness
items.strategy: Use the Artin-Rees comparison of induced and intrinsic filtrations to bootstrap injectivity from the ideal quotient level to all higher powers, then conclude by the ideal criterion.

items.title: For an $R$-finite module over a local map, flatness on the closed fibre plus the multiplication-map condition implies flatness
items.strategy: Reduce to the ideal-form criterion at the maximal ideal and identify the closed-fibre hypotheses with the required flat quotient and injectivity conditions.

items.title: A finite flat module over a local ring is free
items.strategy: Lift a basis of the residue-field quotient to generators, apply Nakayama, and use the equational criterion inductively to show that no nontrivial relation survives.

items.title: A finite flat module over a Noetherian ring is finite projective
items.strategy: Localize at maximal ideals to obtain finite free modules, then apply the finite-projective characterization of finitely presented modules that are locally free.

items.title: Every flat ring map satisfies going down
items.strategy: Localize at the upper prime, use that flat local maps are faithfully flat, and then lift the smaller prime from the localized source through the surjectivity-on-spectra criterion.

items.title: A polynomial algebra is free and therefore faithfully flat over its coefficient ring
A proper localization is flat but need not be faithfully flat
A fraction field is flat over its domain and may fail to be projective
A quotient by an idempotent ideal is flat
The quotient by a nonidempotent ideal is not flat
A finite product of principal localizations covering the spectrum is faithfully flat
A residue-field basis lifts to a basis of a finite flat module over a local ring
